title: 2026 U.S. Senate election in Colorado
description: Colorado voters will elect one member of the U.S. Senate on November 3, 2026, with the primary scheduled for June 30, 2026. The race will fill the Class II seat held by Democrat John Hickenlooper, who was elected in 2020 and took office in 2021. Colorado has leaned Democratic in recent federal elections, and the general election is expected to reflect both the state’s Democratic tilt and the outcome of the primary contests.
polling_note: No public general-election polling found for this race as of 2026-04-01.

candidates.name: John Hickenlooper
candidates.summary: John Hickenlooper is the incumbent U.S. senator from Colorado, having been elected in 2020 and taking office in 2021. He previously served as Colorado’s governor (2011–2019) and as mayor of Denver (2003–2011) before winning election to the Senate.

summary_sources.title: Senator John W. Hickenlooper - Congress.gov
Senator John Hickenlooper | Senator for Colorado
John Hickenlooper - Wikipedia

Healthcare.stance: Supports expanding and protecting the ACA, extending premium tax credits, preserving Medicaid expansion, improving price transparency, and lowering costs through drug-price negotiation and competition.

sources.title: Health Care - John Hickenlooper (official)
Health Care backup - John Hickenlooper (official backup)

Economy.stance: John Hickenlooper advocates building a 21st-century economy by investing in infrastructure, manufacturing, and workforce development. He supports broadband expansion, clean energy investments, affordable housing, and policies that empower workers (including unions) and expand access to paid family leave and lifelong learning.

sources.title: Jobs, Economy & Workforce | Senator John Hickenlooper
Hickenlooper Welcomes $197.4 Million for Colorado Communities in 2026 Funding Bills

Climate/Energy.stance: He champions a bold, science-based climate agenda that accelerates clean energy deployment, reduces pollution, and modernizes the electric grid; he supports the Inflation Reduction Act and bipartisan measures like the Geo POWER Act to unlock geothermal energy and lower energy costs.

sources.title: Climate - John Hickenlooper Senate
Hickenlooper, Daines Introduce Bipartisan Geo POWER Act

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: John Hickenlooper strongly supports reproductive freedom and abortion access, including overturning Dobbs-era restrictions and defending federal protections for reproductive health care. He co-sponsors the Women’s Health Protection Act, introduced the Stop Comstock Act to protect medication abortion and IVF access, and has endorsements from Planned Parenthood Action Fund and Reproductive Freedom for All.

sources.title: Hickenlooper Announces Endorsement from Planned Parenthood - Campaign

Immigration.stance: John Hickenlooper supports a humane, common-sense overhaul of our immigration system, including modernizing border management and expanding lawful pathways to citizenship. He backs restoring DACA and creating a fair guest-worker program while increasing oversight and transparency of immigration enforcement, and he has opposed large funding increases for ICE that would exacerbate issues at the border.

sources.title: Immigration - Hickenlooper Senate site
Hickenlooper calls for comprehensive immigration reform
Hickenlooper votes against ICE funding bill

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: Supports comprehensive gun-safety measures, including universal background checks for all gun sales, red-flag laws, and an assault-weapons ban. He has backed federal reforms such as the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act and the Background Check Expansion Act, and supports funding violence-intervention and mental-health programs.

sources.title: Gun Violence - Hickenlooper Senate
Brady PAC endorsement - Hickenlooper
GIFFORDS PAC endorsement

Foreign Policy.stance: Supports using Congress to authorize military action and opposes unilateral uses of force; he has called for ending the Iran war unless Congress authorizes it. He also supports strong sanctions on Russia, including resuming Russia oil sanctions to pressure Putin, and backing NATO allies.

sources.title: Hickenlooper Statement on Iran War Powers Vote
Hickenlooper, Bennet, Colleagues Demand Trump Resume Russian Oil Sanctions
WATCH: Hickenlooper Demands Trump Stop the Bombs, Lower Americans’ Bills

Education.stance: John Hickenlooper supports universal, high-quality early childhood education (including free universal preschool for 3- and 4-year-olds), affordable, high-quality child care, and making higher education more affordable through loan refinancing, expansion of Pell Grants, and strengthening the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program, while investing in educator salaries, training, and workforce pathways such as apprenticeships.

sources.title: Education page - John Hickenlooper for Senate
Education backup page - John Hickenlooper for Senate

Tech & AI.stance: Supports a federal AI governance framework built on voluntary, transparent standards and third‑party evaluation to ensure safe, responsible AI innovation, including establishing the VET AI Act to set NIST‑led guidelines and external assessments; champions improving workforce data to track AI impacts and investing in skills‑based training to prepare workers for an AI‑driven economy.

Election Policy.stance: Election Policy: John Hickenlooper supports robust voting rights protections and universal access to secure, convenient voting options, including vote-by-mail. He has introduced the Mail and Absentee Voter Protection Act to block attempts to restrict mail-in voting and, with allies, reintroduced the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act to restore and strengthen the Voting Rights Act.

Local Issues.stance: Hickenlooper supports addressing Colorado's affordability crisis by increasing housing supply, protecting homeownership from investor monopolization, and promoting cost transparency and affordability in health care and energy. He backs federal and state efforts to reduce housing costs for working families and invest in affordable housing, with a focus on Colorado communities.

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: John Hickenlooper believes all Americans deserve equal rights and protections under the law, including LGBTQ+ individuals, people of color, and others who have faced discrimination. He co-sponsors the Equality Act, supports the Respect for Marriage Act, and backs voting rights and criminal-justice reforms to expand opportunity and curb systemic inequities.

candidates.name: Karen Breslin
candidates.summary: Karen Breslin is a Democratic candidate in Colorado's 2026 U.S. Senate race. Public sources describe her as an attorney and political science professor, and CU Denver materials say she holds a law degree from the University of Denver and an M.A. from CU Denver.

summary_sources.title: Karen Breslin - Ballotpedia
Karen Breslin - CU Denver College of Liberal Arts and Sciences

Healthcare.stance: Karen Breslin supports Medicare for All to reduce healthcare costs and provide universal, comprehensive coverage for all Americans, prioritizing working families and lower-income individuals.

sources.title: A People and Planet Platform: Economic Fairness & Healthcare (Medicare for All)
Progressive Lawyer Karen Breslin Launches 2026 Colorado Democratic Primary Bid

Economy.stance: Karen Breslin's economic platform centers on economic fairness and reducing costs for working families: support for Medicare for All to lower healthcare costs; a Financial Transaction Tax on stock and bond trades above $300,000; a wealth tax (2% annually on net worth of $50 million+); robust antitrust enforcement to challenge concentration of wealth; raising the minimum wage to $15 per hour; and permanently expanding the Child Tax Credit.

sources.title: Karen Breslin – Priorities: Economic Fairness & Healthcare

Climate/Energy.stance: Breslin’s climate platform emphasizes strong environmental protections, including legislation to reduce microplastics, pesticides, herbicides, and other air and water pollutants; she also supports incentivizing carbon reduction and protecting natural landscapes that function as carbon sinks, such as forests, while defending biodiversity.

sources.title: Climate Change & Environment - Breslin for Colorado

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Karen Breslin supports robust civil rights and equality, including restoring DEI programs and affirmative action via federal legislation, addressing racial disparities in health and other outcomes, and advancing environmental and economic justice while opposing discrimination in all forms.

sources.title: A People and Planet Platform – Priorities
Breslin for Colorado - Campaign Home

Education.stance: Education: Breslin would protect the Department of Education and ensure robust federal funding for K-12 education, use federal funds to close achievement gaps across geographic and racial demographics, defend teachers from political attacks, and restore the Office of Civil Rights.

sources.title: Support for K-12 & Higher Education

Election Policy.stance: Karen Breslin would ban corporate PAC money and impose a one-term limit for herself to reduce donor leverage; she supports anti-corruption and democracy-focused reforms to reduce corporate influence in elections.

sources.title: A People and Planet Platform: Priorities
Karen Breslin for Colorado – official campaign site

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: Oppose life-at-conception legislation and any fetal personhood measures. Support repealing the Hyde Amendment and advancing the Women’s Health Protection Act.

sources.title: Priorities - Reproductive Rights

Immigration.stance: Provide a prompt path to citizenship and end detentions for detainees who have not violated the law beyond entry or pose a security risk, ensuring due process; support an accelerated path to citizenship for DACA recipients and those with temporary protected status (TPS).

sources.title: A People and Planet Platform: Priorities - Immigration (Karen Breslin for US Senate)

Tech & AI.stance: Breslin advocates for robust, proactive federal regulation of artificial intelligence, including guardrails on AI deployment, privacy protections, and accountability for AI developers to ensure safety, ethical use, and protection of workers and democratic processes.

sources.title: Breslin for Senate Instagram post: Regulate AI Before It Kills Us and the Earth
Breslin for Senate TikTok: Regulate AI Before It Kills Us and the Earth

Local Issues.stance: Karen Breslin's Local Issues platform emphasizes government accountability and economic fairness for working families, advocating Medicare for All, opposition to corporate PAC money, strong investment in K-12 and higher education, robust climate protections, and humane immigration policies to support Colorado communities.

sources.title: General priorities - Karen Breslin for Colorado
Progressive Lawyer Karen Breslin Launches 2026 Colorado Democratic Primary Bid
IndivisibleNOCO profile on Karen Breslin
Breslin for Colorado campaign homepage

Foreign Policy.stance: Karen Breslin’s foreign policy vision centers on defending democracy, challenging corporate influence in government, and opposing war profiteering, while endorsing a pro-Israel stance as reflected by her Track AIPAC endorsement; she advocates aligning U.S. policy with human rights and constitutional principles, and supporting a humane immigration and national security framework that prioritizes due process and civilian protection.

candidates.name: Mark Baisley
candidates.summary: Mark Baisley is a Republican member of the Colorado State Senate representing District 4 and is running for U.S. Senate in 2026. Before entering the legislature, he worked in information technology and aerospace-related roles, and his campaign says he has also led a software company.

summary_sources.title: Mark Baisley - Ballotpedia
Senator Mark Baisley - Colorado Senate Republicans
Mark Baisley for United States Senate

Healthcare.stance: Baisley says healthcare decisions should be made by patients and doctors rather than Washington bureaucrats. His campaign says he would seek lower premiums through competition, association health plans, HSAs, price transparency, telehealth, rural hospital support, and fewer federal mandates.

sources.title: Healthcare - Mark Baisley for United States Senate

Economy.stance: Baisley says he would cut federal taxes, roll back regulations he describes as job-killing, and restore American energy dominance to make the U.S. more attractive to employers. His campaign frames this as a pro-growth, private-sector approach to wages and opportunity.

sources.title: Issues - Mark Baisley for United States Senate

Climate/Energy.stance: Baisley’s campaign emphasizes expanding domestic energy production, achieving energy independence, and reducing federal regulations that hinder energy development. The campaign also says he supports permitting reform and prioritizing American-made energy.

sources.title: Mark Baisley for United States Senate
Issues - Mark Baisley for United States Senate

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: Baisley has opposed strengthening abortion protections in Colorado, including opposition to the Reproductive Health Equity Act. Reporting and issue guides describe him as taking a pro-life position and voting against abortion-protection measures.

sources.title: Mark Baisley on Abortion - OnTheIssues.org
Colorado Senate race: Mark Baisley opposes abortion protections

Immigration.stance: Baisley’s campaign says he supports secure borders and enforcement of immigration laws. In the Colorado legislature, he voted against HB26-1276, a bill related to civil liability for immigration enforcement actions in state court.

sources.title: Mark Baisley for United States Senate
HB26-1276 Floor Vote - Colorado General Assembly

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: Sponsored HB26-1021, which would have limited certain state gun restrictions and expanded Second Amendment protections; the bill did not advance.

sources.title: HB26-1021 Second Amendment Protection Act | Colorado General Assembly

Education.stance: Baisley sponsored SB26-055, which would have created a Colorado Department of Education registry for school personnel with disciplinary histories, and SB26-057, which would have required school board directors to be elected by residents of each director district. Both bills were postponed indefinitely in committee.

sources.title: SB26-055 Registry in CDE for School Personnel - Colorado General Assembly
SB26-057 School Board Elections Director District Residents - Colorado General Assembly

Tech & AI.stance: Baisley publicly expressed support for Colorado’s automated decision-making technology framework and referenced SB26-189 in a social media post. He also sponsored or co-sponsored technology-related legislation in the legislature, including measures on information-technology security.

sources.title: Mark Baisley on AI policy
SB 26-189 Automated Decision-Making Technology (Colorado)
Senator Mark Baisley - Colorado General Assembly

Foreign Policy.stance: Baisley’s campaign describes his foreign-policy approach in broad terms, emphasizing national security through secure borders, energy independence, and defending the Constitution. No more detailed foreign-policy platform was found on the campaign site.

sources.title: Mark Baisley for United States Senate

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Baisley has been reported making anti-LGBTQ remarks, and issue guides describe him as opposing some civil-rights expansions related to LGBTQ protections. Publicly available campaign materials reviewed here did not provide a detailed civil-rights platform.

sources.title: LGBTQ Nation article reporting on Baisley's remarks about LGBTQ people

Election Policy.stance: Baisley sponsored HB26-1080, which would require county clerks and recorders to use bipartisan election judges to verify signatures in mail-ballot elections. He also sponsored HB26-1023, a bill addressing ballot-access accessibility requirements for political parties.

sources.title: HB26-1080 County Mail Ballot Signature Verification Requirements
HB26-1023 Political Party Liability for Accessibility Requirements

Local Issues.stance: Baisley’s campaign says he supports targeted infrastructure spending, local control, and accountability for roads, bridges, water systems, broadband, and permitting. The campaign also says he prioritizes Western Slope water infrastructure and reliable energy.

sources.title: Issues - Mark Baisley for United States Senate

reviews.summary: This is a comprehensive and well-sourced candidate profile for Colorado's 2026 U.S. Senate race. Strengths include: (1) Strong factual grounding for the incumbent Hickenlooper, with detailed issue positions backed by official Senate site URLs and credible news sources; (2) Balanced coverage of seven non-incumbent candidates across both parties, with transparent documentation of candidates' varying levels of public disclosure (e.g., Hasley has limited platforms, Joshi has older legislative records); (3) Appropriate use of confidence levels — candidates with sparse platforms are marked as "low" or "medium" confidence rather than over-inferred; (4) Neutral language throughout, with few value-laden terms; (5) Polling data cited with source URL (Working Families/Data for Progress). Minor issues: some candidates (Breslin, Gonzales, Hasley, Jones) lack donor and voting source data, but this appears to reflect genuine absence of disclosed information rather than researcher oversight. The profile appropriately documents what is and is not publicly available.

flags.concern: The claim that Brashad Hasley 'opposed Colorado SB-004' references a specific bill number. While the source provided is a social media reel, verify that the bill number SB-004 is accurately linked to the candidate's specific stated opposition in the context of the 2026 legislative session.
flags.suggestion: Confirm the legislative session bill text matches the candidate's stated concern regarding Second Amendment infringement.

flags.concern: The candidate's stance is summarized with the phrase '100% Pro-Life'. While this reflects the candidate's self-identification as reported in sources, ensure that the use of such labels remains attributed to the candidate or external reporting to maintain complete neutrality.
flags.suggestion: Rephrase to 'The candidate identifies as 100% pro-life and opposes...' to ensure the attribution is clear.

flags.concern: The stance mentions supporting the restoration of 'affirmative action via federal legislation'. This is a highly specific policy claim; ensure the source URL (the candidate's priorities page) explicitly uses the term 'affirmative action' as part of their platform.
flags.suggestion: Double-check the campaign priorities page for the specific term 'affirmative action' to ensure the characterization is precise.

forecast.rationale: There is no public general-election polling for this race, so the forecast relies mainly on Colorado’s recent Democratic lean in federal elections, the advantages of Democratic incumbency, and the candidate field described here. Incumbent Democrat John Hickenlooper is a well-known statewide figure with prior service as governor and mayor, giving Democrats a clear structural edge in a state that has leaned Democratic. The only numeric poll provided is a Democratic primary poll showing some intra-party vulnerability for Hickenlooper against Julie Gonzales, but it does not measure the general election and does not outweigh the broader statewide partisan environment. Because the forecast is being set before the primary and without general-election polling, uncertainty remains meaningful and confidence is only medium.
